abstract: Anton Korinek lays out a scenario-planning framework for economists and policymakers facing the possibility of human-level AI. Distinguishes scenarios ranging from business-as-usual (gradual GPT-style diffusion) to transformative AGI, each with sharply different implications for output, wages, and labor share. Core argument: economists should prepare contingency policy across the scenario set — labor displacement, education reform, market regulation, macroeconomic stability, and international AI governance — rather than betting on any single trajectory. Foundational essay for the scenario-planning approach later operationalized by RAISE US and similar institutional efforts.
keyFindings: Articulates a scenario-planning rather than point-forecast approach to AI economic policy
Identifies labor displacement, education reform, market regulation, macroeconomic stability, and international AI governance as the five policy domains needing contingency plans
Argues output and wage implications diverge sharply across scenarios — institutional design must work across the range
Anticipates the institutional response model (multi-stakeholder coalitions, state-by-state experimentation) later adopted by RAISE US in 2026
Influential in IMF and central-bank AI policy thinking
methodology: Scenario-planning essay for IMF Finance & Development, drawing on Korinek's broader academic work on AI macroeconomics.
qualifiers: Tier 2 — published in IMF Finance & Development (institutional venue but not peer-reviewed in the academic sense). Conceptual framing; specific scenario probabilities are not estimated. Korinek has since joined Anthropic as their economist, which readers may want to weigh.
